notes: Briefs as written by the user on 2026-10-25. Tempo, meter, arrangement, structure and vocal assignments are creative targets: the plan records them, the engine is not guaranteed to follow them.

Instruments are mapped onto the app's vocabulary (felt piano -> piano, tenor saxophone -> saxophone, French horns -> brass section, electronic or hip-hop drums -> drum machine, light drums -> light percussion, live drums -> drum kit).

flavour is a short musical note that goes into the caption; theme is what the songwriter writes about. Lyrics are written by the smart planner (real Claude) with each supplied hook kept unchanged in every chorus.

require_sections names the sections a brief asks for (a bridge, a pre-chorus, the cinematic pullback); the song map never drops them to fit the length. #11 also requires the chorus so that it returns after the breakdown (every lyrical song needs a returning chorus).

takes.title: River waking up
takes.brief: River waking up — expressive Indian flute. 120 seconds, approximately 78 BPM, gentle 4/4. Lead bansuri with tanpura, delicate tabla and occasional santoor. Begin with a spacious flute introduction, introduce a graceful recurring melody, then develop it with ornamentation, breath-shaped phrases and a few fluid runs. Tabla should support the flute without crowding it. End by returning quietly to the opening idea. No voices. Aim for the warmth and expressive playing we loved in Yamuna at Dawn.
takes.flavour: tabla supports the flute without crowding it, ending quietly on the opening melody
targets: development with ornaments, breath-shaped phrases, a few fluid runs
quiet return to the opening idea

takes.title: Midnight café
takes.brief: Midnight café — small jazz ensemble. 90 seconds, approximately 116 BPM, swinging 4/4. Tenor saxophone, Rhodes piano, upright bass and brushed drums. Establish a catchy sax theme, leave space for a short piano answer, then return to the theme. Relaxed, playful and rhythmically alive. Avoid a constant wall of soloing. No voices.
takes.flavour: catchy tenor sax theme, short Rhodes answers, then the theme returns; no wall of soloing

takes.title: Rise of the mountain
takes.brief: Rise of the mountain — cinematic adventure. 120 seconds, approximately 140 BPM, 4/4 with a broad half-time opening. Cello, strings, French horns/brass, taiko and restrained synth bass. Start with a low motif, build through rhythmic strings and percussion, briefly pull back, then deliver an uplifting final statement. Memorable thematic development rather than continuous impacts. No voices.
takes.flavour: broad half-time opening on a low cello motif, brief pullback, uplifting final statement
targets: build through rhythmic strings and percussion
thematic development rather than continuous impacts

takes.title: Lanterns in the rain
takes.brief: Lanterns in the rain — delicate chamber waltz. 90 seconds, approximately 66 BPM, 3/4. Felt piano, cello, harp and soft strings. Tender, slightly wistful, with a lilting pulse. Piano introduces the melody; cello answers and eventually carries it. Keep the arrangement spacious and give it a complete ending. No voices.
takes.flavour: chamber waltz, felt piano introduces the melody, cello answers then carries it, complete ending
targets: cello answers and later carries it

takes.title: थोड़ी देर और
takes.brief: थोड़ी देर और — Hindi romantic male solo. 150 seconds, approximately 76 BPM, 4/4. Acoustic guitar, felt piano, warm bass, brushed drums and final-chorus strings. Intimate verses, a higher melodic chorus, vulnerable bridge and warmer final return. Hook: “थोड़ी देर और मेरे पास रह / जो कह न सके, वो आज कह”. Natural Devanagari Hindi, connected singing and clear consonants. Avoid spoken narration.
takes.flavour: connected singing with clear consonants, never spoken; strings only in the final chorus
hook: थोड़ी देर और मेरे पास रह
जो कह न सके, वो आज कह
takes.theme: A man asks the one he loves to stay a little longer, so that what neither of them could say is finally said today. Intimate verses with small everyday details, a chorus that rises, a vulnerable bridge, a warmer final return.
targets: natural Devanagari Hindi, connected singing, clear consonants, no spoken narration

takes.title: बात अधूरी
takes.brief: बात अधूरी — Hindi female ghazal-inspired song. 120 seconds, approximately 68 BPM, gentle 6/8. Harmonium, sarangi, tabla and restrained acoustic guitar. Poetic but understandable language, elegant melodic turns and breathing space between lines. Hook: “बात अधूरी रहने दे / आँखों को कुछ कहने दे”. Prioritize graceful singing over excessive ornamentation.
takes.flavour: graceful melodic turns with light ornaments, breathing space between lines
takes.theme: A woman asks that a conversation be left unfinished and that the eyes say the rest. Poetic but understandable Hindustani, ghazal-like couplets that each stand on their own.

takes.title: यहीं कहीं
takes.brief: यहीं कहीं — Hindi male/female duet. 150 seconds, approximately 88 BPM, 4/4. Piano, acoustic guitar, bass, light drums and strings. Male verse, female answering verse, shared chorus, contrasting bridge and final duet. Give each character a distinct perspective and appropriate Hindi grammar. Shared hook: “तेरे मेरे बीच कहीं / घर मिला है यहीं कहीं”. Request clear vocal handoffs; report that separation remains unverified until audition.
takes.flavour: clear handoffs: male verse, female answering verse, shared chorus, both voices in the final chorus
takes.theme: Two people find that home is somewhere between them. He describes it from his side, she answers from hers with a different view; together they sing the chorus. The bridge contrasts (a doubt or a memory) before the final duet.
targets: distinct perspectives with correct Hindi gender grammar
clear vocal handoffs (separation unverified until audition)

takes.title: Run Toward the Light
takes.brief: Run Toward the Light — English male rock anthem. 120 seconds, approximately 132 BPM, 4/4. Electric guitars, bass, live drums and restrained organ. Quiet determination in the verse, rising pre-chorus, powerful sung chorus and a brief guitar response. Motivational without generic slogans or constant shouting. Hook: “One more step into the light / I’m still here, I’m still in the fight”.
takes.flavour: quiet determined verses, rising pre-chorus, powerful sung chorus, a brief guitar response
hook: One more step into the light
I’m still here, I’m still in the fight
takes.theme: Someone keeps going after being knocked down: quiet determination, specific images of the struggle, no generic slogans; the chorus is sung with power, not shouted.
targets: no generic slogans, no constant shouting

takes.title: My Own Sunrise
takes.brief: My Own Sunrise — English female motivational soul-pop. 120 seconds, approximately 96 BPM, syncopated 4/4. Rhodes, rounded bass, tight drums, handclaps and backing harmonies. Start vulnerable and grow into confident, joyful singing. Include a sparse bridge. Hook: “I can be my own sunrise / Watch me open up the skies”. Test expressive phrasing and harmonies without burying the lead.
takes.flavour: syncopated soul-pop, starts vulnerable then grows joyful, harmonies never bury the lead
hook: I can be my own sunrise
Watch me open up the skies
takes.theme: A woman moves from doubt to self-belief: the verses start vulnerable and concrete, the chorus is confident and joyful, the bridge is sparse and quiet before the last chorus.
targets: starts vulnerable, grows confident and joyful
backing harmonies without burying the lead

takes.title: आज की रात
takes.brief: आज की रात — Hindi female-led party song. 120 seconds, approximately 124 BPM, 4/4. Dhol, dholak, electronic drums, synth bass, bright brass and group responses. Immediate rhythmic identity, playful verses and an easy sing-along chorus. Hook: “आज की रात खुल के जी / दिल की धुन पे चल पड़ी”. Celebratory and danceable, with a short percussion break and final chorus.
takes.flavour: immediate rhythmic identity, group call-and-response, short percussion break before the final chorus
hook: आज की रात खुल के जी
दिल की धुन पे चल पड़ी
takes.theme: A woman leads her friends onto the dance floor for one free, joyful night; playful verses, an easy sing-along chorus with group responses.
targets: easy sing-along chorus with group responses

takes.title: After the Rain
takes.brief: After the Rain — English female vocal EDM. 150 seconds, approximately 126 BPM, 4/4. Four-on-the-floor kick, sidechain-style pulsing bass/pads, arpeggiated synth and bright melodic lead. Sung verse, emotional pre-chorus, chorus/build, instrumental melodic drop, breakdown and returning final drop. Hook: “After the rain, we come alive / Your hand in mine, electric skies”. The drop should develop the song’s musical identity. Keep intelligible lyrics away from the busiest passages.
takes.flavour: four-on-the-floor kick, sidechain pulse, melodic instrumental drops, vocals kept out of the drops
hook: After the rain, we come alive
Your hand in mine, electric skies
takes.theme: Two people step out after a storm and feel alive again together; the verse is intimate, the pre-chorus emotional, the chorus lifts into the drop.
targets: instrumental melodic drop developing the hook
intelligible lyrics away from the busiest passages

takes.title: अपनी राह
takes.brief: अपनी राह — Hindi male rap with a sung hook. 120 seconds, approximately 92 BPM, 4/4. Hip-hop drums, 808 bass, piano motif and subtle sarangi. Conversational rap verses about steady effort and setbacks, contrasted with a genuinely sung chorus. Hook: “धीरे सही, मैं चल रहा / अपनी कहानी लिख रहा”. Clear Hindi, internal rhymes and rhythmic variation. Spoken-style delivery belongs in the rap verses; the chorus must be melodic.
takes.flavour: conversational rap verses with internal rhymes, a genuinely sung melodic chorus, subtle sarangi
takes.theme: A young man raps about steady effort and setbacks in everyday detail, and sings that slowly but surely he is writing his own story.
